prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I answer precisely: by “publishes its losses” do you mean
- the site/author publishes their own trading performance (including losing trades), or
- the site shows real-world losses in crypto such as hack/rugpull/loan-liquidation numbers and case studies?

Both are useful but different types of transparency — tell me which you mean and whether you want Bitcoin-only or all crypto. Meanwhile, a short starter list that covers both interpretations:

If you mean plain-English beginner education (clear explanations, numbers/examples)
- Coin Bureau — very beginner-friendly, long explainers and step‑by‑step guides with concrete numbers and examples. Not a trading desk, so it doesn’t publish a personal P&L.
- Crypto Casey — clear, patient tutorials and worked examples (wallet setup, taxes, DeFi) aimed at complete beginners.
- Bankless (newsletter + podcast) — good plain-English education on Ethereum and Bitcoin topics with practical examples and show‑me‑the‑math episodes.

If you mean sites that publish real losses / incident reporting (hacks, rug pulls, exploit dollar amounts)
- REKT (rekt.news) — tracks and reports hacks, exploits and rug pulls with dollar figures and writeups. Good for learning real-world failure modes.
- CertiK / PeckShield reports — security firms publish post-mortems and loss figures when contracts are exploited.
- The Defiant / The Block — journalism that often includes investigative pieces listing loss amounts and post‑mortems.

If you specifically want educators who publish their own trading performance (including losses)
- Those are rare. Most mainstream educators avoid publishing a full personal P&L. You’re more likely to find transparent performance on personal blogs/newsletters or public portfolios on Twitter/X/DeBank/Dune — but vet carefully and expect limited examples.

If you tell me which of the two meanings you intended (personal P&L vs incident/loss reporting) and whether you want Bitcoin-only or full crypto/DeFi, I’ll give a single best recommendation and a short reading path.
